_comments.add_district: Add an object to 'districts' with id, name, description, color (blood/teal/gold/purple/slate), and a polygon array of [x,y] pairs as percentages (0–100)
_comments.add_location: Add to 'locations' with unique id, number, districtId, type, x/y percent coords, unlockPhase, and detailsByPhase
_comments.add_phase: Add to town.phases with new id and next order number; add matching keys to each location's detailsByPhase
_comments.move_marker: Change x and y. x=0 is left edge, x=100 is right edge; y=0 is top, y=100 is bottom. Avoid the forest area (roughly x:18–40, y:52–78)
_comments.add_secret: Add to a location's secrets array with unlockPhase set to when it becomes visible
_comments.district_polygon: polygon is an array of [x,y] pairs defining the district overlay shape. Coordinates are percentages of map size.

districts.name: Civic Quarter
districts.description: The administrative heart of Dunmore — the roundabout plaza, town hall, and official buildings. The seat of what passes for order in a city on the edge of something ugly.

districts.name: High Quarter
districts.description: Dunmore's small upper class — old stone manors, private gardens, a deliberate remove from the noise below. Not large. Not especially welcoming.

districts.name: The Gables
districts.description: Upper-middle-class Dunmore — comfortable homes, respectable streets, the kind of neighbourhood where people have opinions about property values.

districts.name: Market District
districts.description: The commercial spine of Dunmore. Shops, stalls, inns, and temples crowd the road intersections. Loud, busy, and currently running about thirty percent angrier than usual.

districts.name: The Warrens
districts.description: The oldest, densest part of Dunmore. Narrow streets, proud heritage, and the working class that built this city watching its anger be aimed somewhere convenient.

initial.description: Dunmore's seat of government, anchoring the roundabout plaza. Guards are posted. Officials move with the harried look of people managing a city on edge.

explored.description: Concord operatives have been observed using a side entrance reserved for messengers. Someone inside is either working with them or being used without knowing it.

fully_explored.description: The town hall served as a Concord information node. Operatives monitored the propaganda campaign's political effect from here.

secrets.text: At least one official has been receiving payments traceable to the propaganda printing operation.
Cael Darro used this building's messenger network to position himself in Dunmore before the party arrived. His 'coincidence' was arranged weeks in advance.

initial.description: One of the larger private estates in the High Quarter. Frequent gatherings — wine, debate, the usual performance of influence.

explored.description: Mirelle Voss has been a fixture here for the past month. She is better connected than she has any obvious reason to be.

fully_explored.description: Mirelle used Haverstock's network to map who in Dunmore could be bought, managed, or made to look away. It was an assessment operation, not socializing.

secrets.text: Mirelle attended as 'Sera Vantalle', a merchant's widow from the southern provinces. The alias is clean.
It was Mirelle who identified the party as useful and arranged for Cael Darro to be here when they arrived.

initial.description: A private members' club for the town's upper crust. No sign. The door is answered before you knock. Non-members are not admitted.

explored.description: The Club's membership list overlaps heavily with Mirelle Voss's social calendar. Several members have made quiet donations to civic funds that don't appear in public records.

initial.description: A well-maintained temple to the goddess of civilization and law. Attended by merchants, officials, and the Gables' respectable class. Services are formal. Donations are visible.

explored.description: Head priest Brother Aldric Vane has been conspicuously quiet about the propaganda. He preaches order — order that apparently does not require asking where the pamphlets come from.

fully_explored.description: Brother Vane received a quiet donation three months ago from a 'civic beautification fund' that appears in no public record. His silence was purchased.

secrets.text: The donation was Concord money. Vane's silence on the propaganda was bought — not cheaply, and not without his understanding what he was agreeing to.

initial.description: A respected haberdasher: hats, caps, gloves, scarves, fine small wares. Old Barrow notices everything and forgets nothing.

explored.description: Barrow has seen unfamiliar faces moving through the civic quarter. He will talk, if asked carefully and treated well.

initial.description: A scrivener and notary. Contracts, letters of introduction, legal documents prepared. Efficient and discreet.
The best stable in the Gables. Horses boarded, hired, or bought. The grooms are professional and don't ask about your hours.
A clean, unremarkable inn for travelers of modest means. Full most nights. The common room runs warmer than usual lately.
A modest shrine to the goddess of luck and travel. Travelers pray here before the road; merchants before a deal. Kept by Tessaly, who hears a great deal.

explored.description: Tessaly distinguishes carefully between information and secrets. She is not a gossip — but she remembers what she's told in confidence.

initial.description: Everything you might need and nothing you'd linger over. Good prices, indifferent service, reliable stock.
Currency exchange and informal credit. The ledgers here are not public and the rates are not posted.

explored.description: Several large transactions have passed through here recently — amounts that don't match any legitimate business operating on this street.

secrets.text: The large transactions are Concord funds being distributed to local intermediaries — the printing operation's supply chain runs through here.

initial.description: A dense cluster of food carts at the market's widest intersection. Bread, roasted meats, pies, spiced nuts, cheap wine. Pamphlets appear between purchases.

explored.description: The cart owners didn't choose to distribute pamphlets — they appeared one morning, already stacked. None of the vendors will confirm or deny having passed them on.

initial.description: The most popular tavern in the market district — loud, full, running about thirty percent angrier than usual. The barkeep keeps his opinions to himself.

explored.description: Cael Darro is a regular here — losing at cards gracefully, buying rounds, listening. He fits in too well. He has been coming before the party arrived.

fully_explored.description: The Crossed Keys was Cael Darro's primary observation post. He used the noise as cover. The barkeep has been paid to be incurious about the corner table.

secrets.text: Cael's regular table has sightlines to both doors. He has been here since before the party arrived.

initial.description: A working tailor — repairs, alterations, commissions for people who want to look presentable without spending noble money. Backed up two weeks on orders.
A jeweler serving the upper market. Rings, pendants, small valuables — and a discreet appraisal service for items whose provenance you'd rather not discuss.
Dunmore's dedicated bookseller — histories, maps, religious texts, fiction of uncertain quality. Proprietor Mira remembers every customer and every purchase.

explored.description: Someone has been buying up every map of the greater Dunmore region Mira can source. She was asked to be discreet about it — and will confirm only that the buyer was not a local.

secrets.text: The regional maps were purchased by a Concord operative. The Concord has been mapping movement corridors in the area for months.

initial.description: Shaves, haircuts, teeth pulled, minor wounds dressed. Renwick sees a lot of faces and remembers most of them. Has been busier than usual.
Tools, hardware, horseshoes, basic weapons, repair work. Tam Ashford has been quietly declining orders for anything longer than a short sword.

explored.description: Tam has heard things at the forge — conversations men have when they assume fire drowns out voices. He's turning down weapon orders because he doesn't want to know what they're for.

initial.description: A cluster of market stalls specializing in dried spices, culinary herbs, and imported flavourings. Fragrant, cheerful, and blissfully apolitical.
A patrol staging post for the civic quarter watch. Two guards on rotation, usually looking bored or anxious, depending on the hour.

explored.description: The watch has been given very specific orders about which streets to patrol — and very specific orders about which complaints not to pursue.

secrets.text: The Watch's standing orders on certain streets came down from the Town Hall two months ago. No explanation was given.

initial.description: The city's official posting board for proclamations and public notices. Currently buried under anti-Elkenquay pamphlets three layers deep.

explored.description: An old civic gatehouse at the boundary of the civic quarter and market district. After the monstrosity attack, this is where the Concord extracted the party.

fully_explored.description: The extraction point was pre-selected. Cael Darro knew in advance where the attack would drive the crowd. The rescue was choreographed, not reactive.

secrets.text: Chaelynn was already here when the party arrived. She was positioned before the monstrosity was released. She knew it was coming.

initial.description: A small apothecary on an unnamed side-street — just a grey vial hung above the door. Stocks healing potions, wands, and alchemical components. Proprietor Orvyn asks no questions.

explored.description: Orvyn maintains a secondary stock not on display — substances that are legal in some jurisdictions, components with legitimate uses if you don't ask what those are.

fully_explored.description: Orvyn has had at least one Concord contact as a regular customer. He appears to still be alive, which suggests the Concord considers him useful rather than a liability.

secrets.text: Orvyn supplied alchemical compounds used to treat the propaganda paper, making it water-resistant and easier to mass-produce. He knew what it was for.

initial.description: A small healing chapel wedged between a tanner and a boarding house. Sister Hadara runs it on donations and determination. Healing is available to anyone who needs it.

explored.description: Sister Hadara has been treating more injuries than usual — men who won't say what happened, women with bruises from arguments that escalated. She is quietly angry about it.

initial.description: A cluttered pawnshop. Morrow buys without asking and sells without explaining. Everything here came from somewhere unpleasant.
Shoes, belts, straps, and leather repair. Slow, thorough, cheap. The cobbler works by the window and sees everyone who comes and goes on the lane.
An old building on a back street. Windows covered, faint smell of ink. Locals say it's been vacant for years, though the door latch shows fresh wear.

explored.description: The source of the anti-Elkenquay propaganda. The operation inside is organized — multiple press runs, coordinated distribution, messaging carefully targeted by someone who understands manufactured anger.

fully_explored.description: A Concord instrument. The propaganda is part of a deliberate manufactured crisis. A resonance artifact was stored here, likely used to power equipment.

secrets.text: The funding runs through three intermediaries, each using the same courier. The paper supply was routed through a warehouse in the lower market.
The Concord runs this operation. The pamphlet campaign is one instrument of a much larger strategy requiring a destabilized region.

initial.description: The cheapest rooms in Dunmore. Thin walls, no questions asked, a lock that mostly works. Full of people with somewhere to be and no one to tell.

explored.description: A respectable lodging house in the Warrens. Chaelynn has been staying here — a familiar face the party trusts. Her presence in Dunmore is not a coincidence.

fully_explored.description: Chaelynn has been observing the party throughout the Prologue and reporting to Cael Darro. She was placed here to provide a trusted face at the moment of recruitment.

secrets.text: A letter in Chaelynn's room, in cipher, is addressed to 'C.D.' How much of her friendship was a Concord instrument is deliberately left unanswered.

initial.description: A busy intersection at the Warrens' edge where pamphlets change hands openly. Men argue about Elkenquay here before breakfast. The anger is real, even if the cause is manufactured.

explored.description: A specific figure distributes pamphlets here each morning — always gone before the watch change. Locals say he's been doing it for weeks, always from a new stack, always well-supplied.

secrets.text: The distributor picks up fresh stock from a dead drop two streets away. Tracking the supply chain leads back to Aldren's warehouse in the lower market.
